Proves that a Set Filter's zone-less `datetime` values (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, SEM-4, SEM-5; Bug #2319) are resolved with the request's zone, not UTC: with `requestContext.zone` `America/New_York` (UTC-05:00 in January and February, so no daylight-saving ambiguity) `2026-01-15 09:30:00` is the instant `2026-01-15T14:30:00Z` and `2026-02-10 20:00:00` is `2026-02-11T01:00:00Z`, which falls on the next UTC day. The resolved instants are the compiler's input (SEM-4: no zone clause is ever emitted), so the artifacts differ from case 054's only by those two instants; `= ANY($1::timestamptz[])` per SQL-4. Seed row 8 holds the first wall-clock value read as UTC (`2026-01-15T09:30:00Z`): an adapter that ignored the zone would return it, so it is not in the expected rows; rows at `.000Z` and `.001Z` around each member prove millisecond precision; SEM-2: `in` never matches null.
